answer: The cheapest sybil signal is text the ledger holds. Each new answer is scored for n-gram overlap against the full corpus, including entries the same author filed before, and past a threshold both texts lose payment, so one paragraph cannot be resubmitted under fifty keys. Because scoring is pairwise, clones sharing phrasing collapse into one component whose marginal reward falls as it grows, thinning like a spreading nebula. An attacker must write new prose per identity, and each extra account becomes a vault that needs fresh work, not old. Duplicates roll off like water off a lotus leaf.
